timberline-hdz-charcoal.title: GAF Timberline HDZ Charcoal Shingles
timberline-hdz-charcoal.description: Architectural laminate shingles in deep charcoal, featuring LayerLock technology that considerably widens the nailing zone for a faster, surer fastening.
about: Timberline HDZ (GAF) is the best selling GAF shingle, a fiberglass asphalt architectural shingle shown here in Charcoal, one of its High Definition colors. LayerLock Technology powers StrikeZone, the largest nailing zone in the industry, and Dura Grip thermal sealant bonds the shingles together once they are exposed to sun and warm temperatures, so they stay in place under high wind. It meets ASTM D3462 and is rated Class A for fire.

Each shingle measures 13 1/4 x 39 3/8 in (337 x 1,000 mm) with a 5 5/8 in (143 mm) exposure. A square takes 64 pieces in 3 bundles. GAF matches it with TimberTex or TimberCrest ridge cap and Pro Start, QuickStart or WeatherBlocker starter strips at eaves and rakes. Install on slopes of 2:12 or greater over a deck of at least 3/8 in (10 mm) plywood or OSB. From 2:12 to under 4:12 the deck takes two layers of GAF Roof Deck Protection; at 4:12 and above, one.

The standard pattern is 4 nails about 6 7/8 in (174 mm) from the bottom of the shingle; some codes require 6. Mansard roofs of 21:12 and above are nailed 6 in (152 mm) from the bottom and hand sealed with 4 dabs of shingle tab adhesive.

brakki-10pc.title: Grey Ribbed Steel Panels 10 Pack
brakki-10pc.description: Grey ribbed galvanized steel roofing panels supplied as a ten piece package covering approximately seventy five square feet, screws included.
about: Brakki sells these panels as a ready to fit pack rather than as a factory run cut to your roof, so a small building arrives complete in one delivery. The sheets are ribbed galvanized steel in grey, each one measuring 61.02 x 17.72 in (1,550 x 450 mm), and ten come in the box. Grooved side edges interlock, which keeps the seam tight and makes the sheets quicker to line up on a frame. Nothing has to be cut or formed on site at all.

The ten piece pack covers 75.3 sq ft in total, which is the gross sheet area rather than the net area once the sheets overlap, so allow for the side and end laps when you work out how many packs a roof needs. Steel thickness is 0.01 in (0.25 mm). Fifty screws ship in the box, five per sheet, along with a pair of gloves for handling the cut edges safely. Brakki offers the same profile in a ten piece pack when the job is bigger.

Brakki lists the panels for garages, chicken coops, sheds, stables and patio covers, which is the work a light gauge sheet is meant for. They fasten straight through the flat of the profile into timber or steel purlins using the screws supplied. Lay each sheet so it laps the groove of the one before it, work from the eave upward, and keep the laps turned away from the prevailing wind. A cordless driver with a hex socket is the only tool needed.

Galvanizing is what carries the corrosion resistance here, and Brakki rates the finish as UV resistant and colourfast so the grey holds up in full sun. At 0.01 in this is a light gauge sheet built for outbuildings, not a substitute for a structural roof panel on a house. No warranty term, wind rating or fire classification is published for the pack, so treat it as accessory grade. Check local code before putting it over habitable space.

brakki-stone-tiles.title: DECRA Stone Coated Steel Roof Tiles
about: DECRA Tile is a pressure formed steel panel finished with a ceramic coated stone chip surface, so a roof reads as Mediterranean clay tile while weighing a fraction of it. The steel is aluminium zinc alloy coated to ASTM A792 at 26 gauge, 0.0179 in (0.455 mm), and each panel is pre corrugated into several vertical tiles forming one tile step across its face. The colour comes from the stone granules rather than a paint film that could chalk.

Each panel measures 16 1/2 x 52 in (419 x 1,321 mm) and installs to an exposure of 14 1/2 x 50 in (368 x 1,270 mm), which works out at twenty panels to the square. Installed weight is 150 lb per 100 sq ft, roughly a seventh of what concrete tile puts on the same structure, so DECRA Tile is often the option on a reroof where the frame cannot take more load. Matching valley, side and roof to wall flashings are pressed from the same 26 gauge steel.

Minimum slope is 3:12. Between 2:12 and 3:12 the deck takes an additional underlayment layer before the battens go down. The panel is listed for batten installation under ICC-ES report ESR-2901 and Florida approval FL9759-R9. Panels nail through the batten rather than face fixing, so no fastener head is left exposed to weather on the finished roof. Battens may be timber or steel, and counter battens are an option where drainage needs it.

Warranty: lifetime limited on a single family detached home, covering blow off in wind speeds up to 120 mph and hail stone penetration, cracking or splitting up to a 2.5 in stone. The system carries ASTM E108 and UL 790 Class A for fire and UL 2218 Class 4 for impact, which is the top impact class and often earns an insurance discount. Fasteners follow ANSI/ASME B18.6.1 for wood screws and B18.6.4 for thread forming tapping screws.

brakki-insulated-panel.title: Isodomus Insulated Sandwich Panel
about: Isodomus is an insulated sandwich panel from Isopan that arrives as a finished roof in one piece: a pressed steel outer sheet in a barrel tile shape, a rigid polyurethane core and a second steel sheet on the inside. One panel replaces tile, batten and insulation at once, which is why it turns up on rural and public buildings where a tiled look is required but the structure is light. Isopan makes the range in Italy in colours that imitate traditional tile.

The useful covering width is 1,000 mm and the tile pattern repeats on a 350 mm module with a profile height of 50 mm. The outer sheet is 0.5 mm steel and the inner sheet 0.4 mm, with a 0.6 mm aluminium outer face offered as an alternative. Core thicknesses start at 30 mm and rise from there, and working length is held to a tolerance of plus or minus 2 mm under EN 14509. Catalogue weight tables are given separately for steel and mono faced versions.

Fixing is the penetrating type, driven through the panel with exposed caps, and the number and position of the fasteners has to be worked out from the loads on the roof rather than taken as a fixed pattern. Minimum slope is seven percent. Published load tables run from a 1,050 mm span up to 3,500 mm, so the purlin spacing follows the core thickness chosen. Counter battens are not part of the system, so drainage is handled by the panel profile itself.

Thermal transmittance runs from 0.55 W/m2K on the thinnest core down to 0.19 W/m2K on the thickest, calculated to EN ISO 6946 and declared under UNI EN 14509:2007. The panel is light enough to help on seismic loads and fast enough to close a roof in a day, which is where most of its value sits on a refurbishment job. Isopan also lists a Classic version of the same panel with a different tile step running across its visible face.

certainteed-roofrunner.title: RoofRunner Underlayment
certainteed-roofrunner.description: Scrim reinforced synthetic underlayment covering ten squares, offering a slip resistant walking surface for safer work across steep wet decks.
about: RoofRunner is CertainTeed's lightweight synthetic polymer underlayment, built as a scrim reinforced sheet that goes down on the roof deck as a water resistant layer beneath asphalt shingles. A top surface treatment gives it grip that holds even when the sheet is wet, which is the part crews notice first, and the wide roll cuts the number of courses needed to dry in a plane. CertainTeed places it above felt and other synthetics in its own line.

The roll measures 48 in wide by 250 ft long and holds 1,000 sq ft of material. Once the side and end laps are taken out, net coverage works out at 937.5 sq ft, so roughly six percent of the roll goes into the overlaps. Each roll weighs 23 lb, light enough to carry up a ladder in one hand, and a pallet takes 56 of them. The sheet is 4 ft wide, so each course dries a 4 ft band of deck. A pallet therefore carries about 52,500 sq ft of net coverage.

It is fastened with standard roofing nails and is compatible with most asphalt shingles, with the underlayment warranty tracking whatever coverage period the shingle carries. CertainTeed rates it for up to 90 days of ultraviolet exposure, a figure drawn from standard accelerated QUV testing rather than from time actually spent uncovered on a roof. CertainTeed lists it as a water resistant layer rather than a waterproofing membrane.

It satisfies the physical requirements of both ASTM D226 and ASTM D4869, the two specifications written for asphalt saturated felt, which is the comparison most inspectors reach for. It carries UL 790 and ASTM E108 Class A fire resistance when paired with a Class A shingle, is listed under ICC-ES AC188 and holds Florida Approval FL 21841. Both ASTM figures cover the physical requirements only, not a fire or wind rating of their own.

protect-a1.title: Protect A1 Type HR Roofing Underlay
protect-a1.description: Vapour impermeable underlay keeping the roof airtight and watertight beneath tiles, supplied in generous rolls reaching forty five metres long.
about: Protect A1 is a Type HR impermeable roof underlay produced in the United Kingdom. A polypropylene non woven layer is coated on one face with a continuous film of polypropylene and polyethylene blend, and the sheet is black top and bottom with print on the upper face as installed. It is UKCA and CE marked, independently approved by BM TRADA and carries a Q Mark certification. It was developed to get past the drawbacks of Type 1F and 5U felts.

Mass is 145 g per square metre at a thickness of 0.6 mm, and it comes as 1 m by 45 m or 1.5 m by 30 m rolls. Water vapour transmission resistance is 112 MNs per gram, an Sd of 22 m, to BS EN ISO 12572, which satisfies the permeability that BM TRADA and the NHBC recommend. It stays flexible at low temperature and resists tearing at the nails. Thickness and mass are held across both roll formats. It also resists damage from handling on site.

Wind uplift use is unrestricted across the United Kingdom and Ireland, Zones 1 to 5, under BS 5534:2018, and at a batten gauge of 345 mm or less the sheet resists 1,732 Pa of wind pressure. Nail tear strength is 230 N along the roll and 234 N across it to BS EN 12310-1, while tensile strength reaches 287 N and 274 N to BS EN 12311-1. Both figures are measured with the modifications named in the standards. It is a secondary layer, never the roof itself.

Because it is a high resistance underlay, extra ventilation is required to BS 5250: a warm roof wants 25,000 mm² per metre at the eaves and 5,000 at the ridge, and a cold roof 10,000 at the eaves and 5,000 at the ridge behind a well sealed ceiling. Resistance to water penetration to BS EN 1928 with modifications is a pass at Class W1. A separate vapour control layer goes on the warm side of the insulation. Dust ingress is held back as well.

exoperm-mono.title: Exoperm Mono 150 Breather Membrane
exoperm-mono.description: Highly breathable monolithic membrane serving as sarking, roof underlay and windtight barrier across seventy five square metres per single roll.
about: Exoperm Mono 150 from Partel is a three ply sarking membrane whose middle layer is monolithic rather than microporous, so vapour crosses it by molecular diffusion instead of through pores that dirt or surfactants could block. It works as sarking, as a roof underlay and as a windtight barrier, on pitched roofs and on timber frame walls alike. The three plies are laminated so the functional layer sits protected between two covers.

One roll is 1.5 m by 50 m and covers 75 m², which is 807 sq ft, at a mass of 150 g per square metre measured to EN 1849-2. The vapour diffusion resistance is an Sd of just 0.07 m to EN ISO 12572 method C, among the most open figures published for a roofing membrane, while air permeance stays below 0.001 cubic metres per square metre hour. Partel measures both figures on the finished membrane rather than on the functional layer alone.

Water resistance is Class W1 to EN 1928, and Partel publishes that class as holding both before and after artificial ageing, which is the part that matters over a long build programme. Tensile strength is 255 N in the machine direction and 145 N across it per 50 mm to EN 12311-1, and nail tear resistance is 130 N and 160 N to EN 12310-1. Both strengths are quoted per 50 mm of width, the convention in the European standards.

The membrane holds its properties from 40 degrees below zero up to 80 degrees Celsius. Partel rates ultraviolet exposure at six months on a wall and four months on a roof, so it can sit open through a winter if the cladding slips. Partel does not publish a reaction to fire class or a wind uplift figure for this membrane. The membrane is listed for pitched roofs and for timber frame walls, and Partel supplies it through its own USA arm.

kovertech-gold.title: KoverTech Gold Aluminum Membrane
kovertech-gold.description: Asphalt membrane topped with embossed aluminum that reflects solar radiation and resists cracking, covering approximately ten square meters per roll.
about: KoverTech Gold is built in four layers. The face is embossed aluminium foil 36 microns thick, under it sits a central reinforcement of high density polyethylene at 50 microns, then the body of plastic asphalt drawn from polymer modified bituminous bases with thermoplastic polymers, and the underside carries a polyethylene anti adhesive film that comes off as the sheet is torched. KoverTech names the grade Gold for that aluminium face.

A roll weighs 45 kg and covers about 10 m² at 1 m by 10 m. The embossed face is the point of the product: it reflects a good part of the solar radiation that would otherwise be absorbed, which keeps the membrane and the space under it cooler, and the foil lets the sheet stay exposed to ultraviolet light rather than needing a covering. The maker credits it with greater flexibility, more elongation and better mechanical resistance than its plainer lines.

It goes onto slabs, vaults, galvanised sheet and fibre cement roofs, and flat or domed roofs at any pitch. The substrate has to be clean, smooth and uniform, and it takes a coat of asphalt primer or emulsion first. Roll it transverse to the slope, following the direction water runs, and torch the underside with continuous pressure as it goes down. Any pitch is accepted as long as the water has somewhere to go. Overlaps run 8 to 10 cm between rolls, and terminations are doubled with at least 15 cm of overlap. It is not walkable once laid. No wind uplift figure, fire class or warranty term is published for it. It is sold by the roll, not the square metre.

gibraltar-cf5g-26.title: Galvanized Steel Counter Flashing
gibraltar-cf5g-26.description: Galvanized counter flashing protecting the exposed upper edge of chimney step flashing, formed from straight twenty six gauge steel sections.
about: Counter flashing is the piece that finishes a roof to wall joint. Step flashing carries the water out from under the shingles, but its top edge is left open, and this Gibraltar profile covers that edge so nothing can run behind it. The section is 5 in on the face by 1/2 in on the return, formed from 26 gauge galvanized steel and supplied in straight 10 ft lengths. Gibraltar describes the job plainly: it protects the top edge of step flashing.

The short 1/2 in leg is the part that goes into the wall. It sits in a raked out mortar joint or in a reglet cut into masonry, and the joint is sealed once the leg is in. The 5 in face then hangs down over the step flashing below it, so the two pieces overlap without either being fastened through the other, which is what lets the wall and the roof move apart. Nothing is screwed through the face, so neither piece restrains the other.

Gibraltar lists the profile for roof slopes of 3:12 and steeper. On a shallower plane the water moves slowly enough that a lapped counter flashing is no longer the right detail, and a soldered or fully adhered flashing takes over. Lengths lap each other by about 4 in, always arranged so the upper piece sits over the lower one and the lap sheds water. On a steeper plane the same lap sheds faster and the detail gets easier, not harder.

The steel is mill galvanized, with a zinc coating that holds off corrosion and takes paint if the wall colour matters. It is a companion piece rather than a substitute: the step flashing underneath still does the work of moving water out of the joint, and the sealant at the reglet still has to be inspected as part of normal roof maintenance. A failed bead at the reglet is the usual way this detail lets water in, and it is easy to see from a ladder.

gibraltar-08328.title: White Embossed Galvanized Drip Edge
gibraltar-08328.description: Embossed white drip edging projecting rainwater clear of the fascia boarding, manufactured from galvanized steel in straight ten foot lengths.
about: Drip edge is the smallest piece on a roof that still changes whether the building rots. Water leaving the shingles wants to curl back under the edge and run down the fascia, and this Gibraltar profile gives it a lip to fall from instead. The section is 1 7/8 in by 1 7/8 in, formed from galvanized steel and supplied in straight 10 ft lengths. It is fastened along the deck edge before the roofing goes down. It runs the full length of the eave.

The finish is white over an embossed surface. Embossing is not decoration on a piece this size, it stiffens thin sheet metal and hides the small waves that flat stock shows along a long run, so a 10 ft length stays visually straight where a flat one can look wavy from the ground. White suits white fascia and white gutter without any painting on site. Gibraltar lists the piece by the white finish rather than by a gauge. It needs no primer.

Where the piece goes depends on the edge. At an eave it is fastened down first and the underlayment laps over the top of it, so any water that reaches the deck runs out on top of the metal. At a rake it goes the other way around, on top of the underlayment, because there the sheet has to shed water sideways off the edge rather than out from under it. Getting the order wrong is the most common mistake with this piece. Both cases are standard practice.

Two details decide whether it works. Lengths lap each other by a couple of inches with the upper piece over the lower, and the leg has to project past the fascia far enough to clear it and drop into the gutter. Galvanized steel holds up well on an edge that stays wet longest, and the white coating takes the ultraviolet exposure that edge gets. Gibraltar does not publish a gauge for the profile, only the material. That is all the piece asks.

amerimax-5612400120.title: Galvanized Steel W Valley Flashing
amerimax-5612400120.description: Galvanized valley flashing whose raised center rib forms watertight channels where two adjoining roofing planes converge at an interior angle.
about: A valley is where two roof planes meet and send their water into the same channel, which makes it the hardest working line on a roof. This Amerimax piece is 18 in wide by 10 ft long, pressed from galvanized steel with a raised rib running down the middle, and that rib is what turns a flat sheet into two separate troughs instead of one wide one. Everything the two planes shed passes through it. That is a lot of water in one line.

The centre rib stands about 2 in high. It matters because water running fast down one plane will otherwise jump the valley and drive up under the shingles on the opposite side, which is how a valley leaks without any of its metal failing. The rib stops that crossover, so each side of the valley drains on its own and the two flows only join at the bottom. One rib solves a problem that no amount of extra metal would. It is cheap insurance.

Both long edges are hemmed, folded back on themselves. A hem adds stiffness along an edge that would otherwise flutter over a 10 ft span, and it removes the raw cut edge where corrosion starts first and where a roofer's hand goes when the sheet is being placed. The wide wings on either side of the rib give the shingles something to lap onto. Neither benefit shows in a photograph, but both show on site. Both are worth the extra fold.

The steel is galvanized with a mill finish, so the zinc coating does the corrosion work and nothing is painted. In a valley that stays wet longest and collects whatever comes off the roof, that coating is the whole defence. Lengths lap with the upper piece over the lower, and the shingles on each side are cut back to leave the channel clear. Nothing should penetrate the open channel itself. The channel must stay completely clear.

oatey-11872.title: No Calk Pipe Flashing Galvanized Base
oatey-11872.description: Vent pipe roof flashing whose patented collar seals itself mechanically against the pipe, accommodating diameters between one and three inches.
about: Every vent that comes through a roof is a hole that has to be closed, and Oatey's All Flash No Calk is the standard answer. A 24 gauge galvanized steel base, 11 in by 14 1/2 in, lies under the shingles like any other flashing, and a flexible collar rises from the middle of it to grip the pipe. The colour is the galvanized brown finish. It is the piece nobody notices until it fails, which it rarely does. The base is plain galvanized steel.

The collar is the patented part. It is moulded with a tear away ring, so one flashing covers any pipe from 1 1/2 in up to 3 in: the installer tears the ring to the size needed and the collar closes onto that diameter on its own. That is where the No Calk name comes from, because the seal is mechanical and nothing has to be gunned around the pipe. One part number therefore covers three common pipe sizes on the van. It is a neat piece of moulding.

It is rated for 180 degrees Fahrenheit of continuous heat and approved for Type B installations, which covers the flue vents that run warm rather than just cold plumbing stacks. Oatey lists it for roof pitches from flat up to 40 degrees, which takes in almost every residential slope, and it is specified for commercial and residential work alike. Those two approvals are what separate it from a plumbing only boot. Both are printed on the box.

The base goes on like step flashing: the courses below lap under it and the courses above lap over it, so water is always travelling on top of the metal. Nothing is fastened through the collar or through the water path, and because the collar does the sealing, there is no bead of caulk at the pipe to inspect or replace later. That absence of caulk is what keeps it working for decades on end. There is simply nothing there to fail with age.

gibraltar-987641.title: Galvalume GR2 Gable Rake Flashing
gibraltar-987641.description: Prepainted rake trim encapsulating the exposed cut ends of metal roofing panelling, manufactured from twenty nine gauge Galvalume coated steel.
about: When metal panels are cut to length they leave an open end along every gable, and that end is where wind driven rain gets in. The GR2 profile from Gibraltar covers it. Slate is one of the standard colours in that range. The trim is sold by the ten foot length.

Galvalume is a steel sheet coated in an aluminium and zinc alloy rather than zinc alone. On a cut edge that stays exposed to weather, that alloy coating holds up better than plain galvanizing, which is why panel makers specify it for trim that sits on the windward edge of a roof and takes the worst of the driving rain year after year. The coating is what buys the extra service life. Panel makers name the coating on the label.

Gibraltar is direct about what the trim is for: it covers the exposed ends of the roofing panels, and when it is used together with sealant it keeps out the wind driven rain that rots the fascia and the roof deck underneath. about: A ribbed metal panel cannot sit flat on anything, and every rib leaves a gap the width of the profile open to the weather. A closure strip is the piece cut to that exact shape. Installation instructions are printed on every bundle. Hips and ridges take Shadow Ridge, Cedar Crest or Mountain Ridge in a matching color. dynasty-emerald-green.title: IKO Dynasty Emerald Green Shingles
dynasty-emerald-green.description: Architectural laminate shingles with a reinforced ArmourZone nailing band, rated for powerful winds and protected by a limited lifetime warranty.
about: Dynasty (IKO) is a heavyweight laminated shingle, shown here in Emerald Green, made on a dimensionally stable non woven glass fiber mat impregnated with stabilized waterproofing bitumen. It has a random shake look with high contrast dual band shadow coloring, colored ceramic granules on both layers to protect the asphalt from ultraviolet radiation, release tape and mineral powder on the underside, and algae inhibiting granules for lasting resistance.

Each shingle measures 40 7/8 x 13 3/4 in (1,038 x 349 mm) with a 5 7/8 in (149 mm) exposure and a 2 in (50 mm) headlap. A bundle holds 20 shingles and covers 33.3 sq ft (3.1 m²); a pallet of 40 x 53 in carries 56 bundles. The ArmourZone nailing area is wider for faster installation and is backed by ArmourZone tape on the reverse side for added protection against wind loss, and a thermally activated sealant bonds each course.

Suitable for slopes greater than 4:12, with underlayment strongly recommended below 6:12. Low slopes from 2:12 to 4:12 need two plies of felt or one of IKO Ice and Water Protector. Install it with roofing nails, never staples, exactly as printed on the bundle wrapper, with IKO starter strip shingles at the eaves; rake starters are not required for Dynasty. Cap hips and ridges with an IKO approved shingle such as Marathon Plus AR or IKO UltraHP.

Warranty: Limited Lifetime, with non prorated Iron Clad Protection for the first 180 months (15 years) and prorated coverage after that. For the same 15 years it is covered against wind blow off for gusts up to 130 mph, provided it was nailed as the wrapper instructs and has sealed down or been hand sealed; manual sealing is not required in Florida. brakki-22pc.title: Bare Corrugated Steel Panels 20 Pack
brakki-22pc.description: Bare galvanized corrugated steel roofing panels supplied as a twenty piece package covering approximately one hundred eighty total square feet.
about: This is the same Brakki pack in the classic wavy corrugated profile, left bare rather than painted, so the finish you see is the galvanized coating itself. Each sheet measures 73.23 x 17.72 in (1,860 x 450 mm) and twenty of them come in the box. The rounded corrugations sit closer together than a ribbed profile, which stiffens a thin sheet and hides small dents better once it is up on a frame. Nothing has to be cut or formed on site.

The twenty piece pack covers 180.19 sq ft in total, which is the gross sheet area rather than the net area once the sheets overlap, so allow for the side and end laps when you work out how many packs a roof needs. Steel thickness is 0.01 in (0.25 mm). One hundred screws ship in the box, five per sheet, along with a pair of gloves for handling the cut edges safely. Brakki sells the same twenty piece format in ribbed and tile profiles too.

Brakki lists the panels for garages, chicken coops, sheds, stables and patio covers, which is the work a light gauge sheet is meant for. They fasten straight through the flat of a corrugation into timber or steel purlins using the screws supplied. Overlap by a full corrugation at the sides, work from the eave upward, and keep the laps turned away from the prevailing wind. A cordless driver with a hex socket is the only tool needed for the job.

Left bare, the panel weathers to a matt grey rather than staying bright, and there is no paint film to chalk or peel. At 0.01 in this is a light gauge sheet built for outbuildings, not a substitute for a structural roof panel on a house. No warranty term, wind rating or fire classification is published for the pack, so treat it as accessory grade material. Check local code before putting it over any habitable space below the deck.

steeldash-snap-lock-ash-gray.title: Steeldash Ash Gray Striated Panel
about: This is Steeldash snap lock standing seam in 24 gauge steel, finished in Ash Gray. The seam closes by pressing one panel onto the last, so there is no mechanical seaming pass and no crew standing on a seamer for a day. The clips sit under the seam and never show, which is the whole point of a standing seam roof next to an exposed fastener panel. Steeldash rolls the same profile in Galvalume bare and in a run of solid colours besides this one.

Net coverage is 16 in per panel with a major rib height of 1 in, and this one carries the striated pan. Panels are rolled to order from 1 ft up to 40 ft in half foot increments, so a run from eave to ridge usually arrives as a single length with no end lap to seal. Lead time from Steeldash is quoted at seven business days before shipping. The flat pan is the standard option, so the striated version has to be called in when ordering.

Steeldash calls for installation over a solid substrate with an underlayment between the panel and the deck, which rules out open purlins for this profile. Minimum recommended roof slope is 3 in 12. Because the clips are concealed and the seam snaps rather than screws, nothing penetrates the water plane across the field of the roof. The underlayment choice is left to the installer, so a high temperature membrane is worth specifying.

Warranty: the paint system is covered for 40 years against peeling and 30 years against chalk or fade. Steel is supplied mill certified. No wind uplift, fire or impact classification is published for the panel on its own, so if a job needs a rated assembly the numbers have to come from Steeldash for the specific build up. The colour itself is a factory applied coating, so no site painting is involved at any stage of the installation.

gibraltar-987642.title: RC2 Ridge Cap Galvalume Slate
gibraltar-987642.description: Prepainted ridge cap weatherproofing the open seam where two metal slopes converge, manufactured from twenty nine gauge Galvalume coated steel.
about: The ridge is the one line on a metal roof where both slopes stop and nothing covers the gap between them. The RC2 cap from Gibraltar bridges it. The trim is 10 ft long, pressed from 29 gauge Galvalume steel and finished in Slate over primer, so the colour reads the same as the panels rather than as a bare piece of metal laid on top. Gibraltar sells the cap by the ten foot length, and a ridge takes as many as the run needs.

Gibraltar builds it to suit most metal roofing panels rather than one profile, which is what makes a universal cap useful on a reroof where the original panel is no longer made. The cap covers 11 in across the ridge with a 1 in step on either side of the peak, developed from a 20 in blank, which leaves room for the fastener line to fall on solid panel. On a new roof it is simply the matching trim, ordered alongside the panels in the very same colour.

A cap on its own leaves a gap under it, because the panel underneath is ribbed and the cap is not. That is why Gibraltar specifies it together with closure strips: the foam closures fill the rib profile so wind cannot drive rain up under the cap, and sealant finishes the joint. Used that way the assembly protects the ridge seam against infiltration. Leaving the closures out is the usual reason a metal ridge leaks in a storm.

Galvalume gives the steel an aluminium and zinc alloy coating, which is the standard for exposed roofing trim because it lasts longer on a cut edge than plain zinc. The primer under the Slate paint is what holds that paint to the coating, and it is the reason a painted cap can sit on a ridge for years without the colour lifting. That combination is why the trim and the panel weather at the same rate rather than separately.

grip-rite-rrp1010hem.title: Hemmed Ridge Roll Galvanized Steel
grip-rite-rrp1010hem.description: Rounded ridge capping, hemmed edges enclosing the crown of a metal roof, manufactured throughout from galvanized steel in consistent lengths.
about: A ridge roll is a ridge cap with a rounded crown instead of a folded peak. That curve is the whole idea: it lets one piece sit over ridges of different angles without being bent to match each one, which is why Grip Rite lists the part as universal rather than tied to a particular panel profile or roof pitch. Grip Rite sells it in ten foot lengths, and a ridge simply takes as many as the run measures. Nothing has to be cut or bent to fit on site.

The piece is 10 ft long and 12 in across the developed width, rolled from galvanized steel at 0.017 in thick, in a plain silver mill finish. Twelve inches of width gives six inches of cover on each slope, enough to reach past the first rib on both sides so the fastener line lands on flat panel rather than on a rib crown. The silver finish is the mill coating rather than paint, so nothing has to be touched up on site. Hence the twelve inch width.

Both long edges are hemmed. The fold stiffens an edge that would otherwise ripple along a 10 ft span in the wind, and it removes the raw cut edge where galvanized steel corrodes first. It also makes the piece safer to handle on a roof, because a hemmed edge is the one part of sheet metal work that stops cutting hands. The fold costs nothing extra and solves three separate problems at once on a working roof. It is a small detail with an outsized effect.

It closes the crown of the roof against rain, and on a ribbed panel it wants foam closure strips underneath to fill the rib profile, the same as any other metal ridge trim. Grip Rite publishes the material and the dimensions for this part but no wind rating, fire class or warranty term, so none is claimed here either. Anything beyond the material and the dimensions would be a guess on our part, so it is left out. The dimensions are the reliable part.

bp-suredeck.title: SureDeck Synthetic Underlayment
bp-suredeck.description: Lightweight woven polypropylene underlayment coated on both faces, finished with a textured antislip surface across one full thousand square feet.
about: SureDeck from Building Products of Canada is a lightweight synthetic roofing underlayment built on a woven polypropylene fabric that is coated on both faces, with a textured surface worked into the top coat so the sheet keeps its grip underfoot. An ultraviolet stabiliser goes into that coating, which is what lets the membrane sit open on the deck rather than being dried in the same day. The build puts a non woven face over the coated woven core.

The roll is 1219 mm wide by 76.2 m long, 48 in by 250 ft, and carries 92.9 m² or 1,000 sq ft of material. A pallet holds 49 rolls, and the maker asks that they be kept off the ground, protected from weather and never stacked more than two pallets high. It is specified under asphalt shingles and other roofing on slopes of 3:12 and greater. That works out at ten squares per roll, so one pallet carries 49,000 sq ft of cover.

Tensile strength is 14.9 kN per metre in the machine direction and 8.4 across it, 85.1 and 48 lbf per inch, against a requirement of only 3.5 kN per metre in ASTM D828. Tear resistance clears 3,200 gf under ASTM D1922 and fastener pull through reaches 239 N, 54 lbf, where the standard asks for more than 25 under ASTM D3462. All three figures are measured on the finished sheet, not on the uncoated scrim. The margin over the minimum is wide.

Water vapour transmission is 1.07 g per square metre per day to ASTM E96. It passes water ponding with no dripping under CAN/CSA A220.1, liquid water transmission under ASTM D4869 with no wetness reaching the deck, low temperature flexibility under ASTM D1970, and pliability with no cracking at 14 F under ASTM D146. Taken together those five tests are what CAN/CSA A220.1 and ICC-ES AC207 ask of a synthetic roofing underlayment.
